notes:
SCOPE / JUDGEMENT CALLS a reviewer must check before import.

1. FRAGRANCE IS HOME-ONLY. catalogue.json names both SKUs 'Home Fragrance' (slugs abk-mashmom-home-fragrance, abk-secret-home-fragrance) while llms.txt says 'home and car fragrances'. Until a car SKU is confirmed I have bid ONLY home-fragrance terms and added 'car perfume' / 'car air freshener' / 'معطر سيارة' as ad-group negatives. If a car fragrance SKU genuinely exists and gets its own page, add a sixth ad group; do not bolt car terms onto this one.

2. FRAGRANCE FORMAT IS UNKNOWN. Both fragrance products have an empty 'specs' field, so nothing tells us whether they are a spray, a diffuser or an oil. Every headline and description in that ad group is deliberately format-neutral ('home fragrance', 'scent', 'blend') and never says spray, bottle, ml or diffuser. Keep it that way until the format is confirmed, otherwise the ad promises a form factor the landing page may not show.

3. FRAGRANCE LANDING PAGE uses the hub filter https://abktradingservice.com/en/b2c/products?category=fragrance (and the /ar/ equivalent) because the ad group covers two SKUs. Verified live: ProductGrid.tsx reads 'brand' and 'category' from useSearchParams, and 'fragrance' is a real category in catalogue.json, so this cannot 404. If you prefer a single-SKU page, point it at abk-mashmom-home-fragrance (the featured one) and drop the 'abk secret' keyword.

4. TWO THEME PRODUCTS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED. (a) ProtectGuard WF Premium is audience:'b2b' with url_b2c_en = null, and its real search demand is stone/concrete/tile sealer - a different vertical from interior car care. It needs its own B2B ad group pointed at https://abktradingservice.com/en/b2b/products/protectguard-wf-premium, not a slot in this campaign. (b) Fast Masking Tape is excluded per the research brief's own recommendation: generic hardware traffic, negligible margin, and every tape query would drag the ad group off-theme.

5. NO SERVICE LANGUAGE ANYWHERE. No headline or description contains install, fitting, book, appointment, service, apply-to-your-car, or تركيب / احجز / موعد / خدمة. The only place a fitting is mentioned is the EN leather description 'your own detailer applies it', which explicitly states ABK does NOT apply it - that is the sanctioned framing from the brief. The Arabic copy avoids the word تركيب entirely rather than using it in a negated sentence, because a negation reads badly in a fast RTL scan.

6. NO PRICES. No headline, description or keyword states, implies or anchors a price. The offer everywhere is 'ask on WhatsApp for a quote' / 'اطلب عرض السعر على واتساب'.

7. ARABIC RTL RULES APPLIED. No Arabic headline starts with a Latin token or a digit; no em-dash or pipe anywhere in Arabic ad text; no terminal punctuation; no tashkeel (catalogue's مركّز / ملمّع are written مركز / ملمع); Western digits only; display paths are Latin ('ar' + topic) because Arabic paths render unpredictably. Arabic headlines are 11-27 chars against the 30 limit, giving the glyph-width headroom the brief asked for. STILL PROOF EVERY ARABIC ASSET IN GOOGLE'S OWN RTL AD PREVIEW BEFORE PUBLISHING - a monospace editor hides bidi faults.

8. PHONE NUMBER IS ENGLISH-ONLY IN COPY. appears in EN descriptions but not in AR descriptions, because a '+' next to an Arabic run is a bidi-neutral character that jumps to the wrong visual edge. Attach a Call asset with at campaign level so the Arabic ads still carry the number.

9. BID STRATEGY. 'Maximize conversions' is set for consistency with the other theme files, but on day one there is no conversion history and the conversion is a human WhatsApp reply. Recommend launching both campaigns on Maximize Clicks with the per-ad-group maxCpcQAR values as the cap, then switching to Maximize Conversions once WhatsApp-click conversions have ~30 recorded actions.

10. AD SCHEDULE is tightened to real trading hours (Sat-Thu 09:30-13:30 and 15:30-22:30, Friday off) rather than a flat 09:00-23:00, because nobody answers WhatsApp during the 13:00-16:00 closure and paying for those clicks wastes a low budget.

11. VERIFIABLE CLAIMS ONLY. 'Made in Canada' and '1:5 dilution' appear only in the Briller interior-cleaner ad group (both are in that product's specs). '50 ml' and 'non-oily' come from the Autotriz Leather & Vinyl record; '300 ml', 'upholstery, carpet and soft tops' from the Fabric & Textile record; '450 ml aerosol', 'penetrates fast', 'emulsifies glue' from the Detainer record. Nothing is claimed for the fragrances beyond 'signature', 'premium' and 'long-lasting', which is exactly what the catalogue says.

12. SHARED NEGATIVES include the bilingual service block, the excluded brands (InstaFinish, Getsun, Sitrett, Grizzly), rival brands, marketplaces, jobs/info queries and the vertical homonyms that matter for THIS theme (hair/dog shampoo, nail and shoe polish, lip and hair tint, salad and wound dressing, salon waxing, compound villas, and the Indian Public Provident Fund). Note the Arabic word مركز is deliberately NOT a negative on its own - it collapses with مركّز ('concentrated') once diacritics are stripped and would suppress the best B2B shampoo and cleaner traffic; only the full phrase مركز تلميع is blocked.
